target: APG focus return exceptions and visible close-button recommendation
observed_behavior: The APG modal pattern describes returning focus to the invoking element when a dialog closes, but specifies exceptions. If the opener no longer exists, focus goes to another logical workflow element. If the completed task leads naturally to a subsequent step and immediate re-invocation is unlikely, another destination can be more logical; its example moves focus into a newly added grid row after an add-rows dialog. Separately, APG strongly recommends including a visible button for closing a dialog in the tab sequence, such as a close icon or Cancel action.
context: W07 B3 K3 read-only APG Keyboard Interaction — Notes 2 and 3; first-party non-normative explanatory guidance, bounded to qualified APG pattern and exceptions.
limitations: Focus return is not absolute, and the documented task-continuation exception must not be erased.
Visible close-button guidance is strong APG recommendation, not itself proof of WCAG conformance or universal visual control placement.
The source describes modal dialog pattern interactions, not browser-native restoration algorithms or runtime test results.
No actual opener destruction, grid workflow, close event or focus restoration was tested.
